beforeSourceBodies.text: Desperate Escape Test 09.07.01Some rules may reference the term 'Desperate Escape test'. In all instances this means the hazard rolls made for the desperate escape mode of a fall-back move.Abilities that subtract from a unit's Desperate Escape test instead subtract from those hazard rolls.Example: A battle-shocked unit makes a fall-back move away from a unit of Bloodletters that have the Bane of Cowards ability. As a result of Bane of Cowards, because the unit making the fall-back move is battle-shocked, the hazard rolls they make as part of their desperate escape will be at -1.

afterSourceBodies.text: Desperate Escape TestSome rules may reference the term 'Desperate Escape test'. In all instances this means the hazard rolls made for the desperate escape mode of a fall-back move.Abilities that subtract from a unit's Desperate Escape test instead subtract from those hazard rolls.If a stratagem or ability instructs a unit to make a Desperate Escape test, that unit:Must use the desperate escape mode when it is selected to make a fall-back move.Must make one hazard roll for each model in that unit.Must make a battle-shock roll.Example 1: A battle-shocked unit makes a fall-back move away from a unit of Bloodletters that have the Bane of Cowards ability. As a result of Bane of Cowards, because the unit making the fall-back move is battle-shocked, the hazard rolls they make as part of their desperate escape will be at -1.Example 2: If an ability allows a unit to re-roll Desperate Escape tests, that unit can re-roll hazard rolls made for the desperate escape mode of a fall-back move.
